punchline: Ask people to imagine a sick girl's feelings and three-quarters will move her ahead of the other children in line.
thirty_sec: In a 1995 experiment Paul Bloom describes, volunteers were asked whether Sheri Summers, a ten-year-old with a fatal disease, should skip ahead on a waiting list. Told first to imagine her feelings, about three-quarters said yes. Without that request, about one in three did. The girl and the list were the same. Bloom's point: empathy lights up one person and leaves the others in line out of sight.
